reasons.Attribute: \"\": N units of the file are: The reader names a measure's unit that is neither a length nor an angle by its entity types ('derived_unit'), which does not identify one of the file's several derived units; the writer will not pick one (it would guess the unit). The attribute set is left out of the round trip.
reasons.Datum: datum … is established by datum t: Datum targets are read but not written yet (design: Out of scope); a datum they establish is refused with them, and tolerances referencing it are left out of the round trip.
reasons.DatumTarget: datum targets are read but: Writing datum targets is out of scope for this stage (design: Out of scope); refused by name.
reasons.Dimension: a dimension without a nominal: NIST CTC-01 states dimensions without a dimensional_characteristic_representation (a nonconformance the reader reads through, pinned in read/findings.json); PMI practice §5.2.1 requires the nominal value, so the writer refuses to write the nonconformance.
reasons.Feature: a group of unstated kind (§N.N: NIST FTC-09's composite_group_shape_aspects state neither 'multiple elements' nor 'pattern of features' (read as GroupKind::Unstated with a finding); writing a group whose kind is not stated would write the nonconformance, so it is refused with what depends on it.
reasons.Hole: hole definitions (basic_round_hole: Edition 4 hole occurrences' basic_round_hole definitions (NIST STC-09) are read into PartPmi.holes, but the writer does not write them yet (docs/step-ap242.md question 7, Q-holes); refused by name so that a replace never drops them silently. The occurrences' faces are still written as their features (the written file is unchanged).
reasons.Note: notes are the non-standard 'manufa: specify-core's 'manufacturing requirement' properties (threads, knurls, finish, edge condition, general tolerances as text) are not a standard AP242 form; maintainer decision 5: not written.
reasons.Tolerance: a projected tolerance zone wi: NIST CTC-04's projected zone names a projection end that identifies no face (read through with a finding); §6.9.2.2 requires the end, so the writer refuses the tolerance rather than write an empty shape aspect.
reasons.ToleranceRelation: tolerance relations (: Writing tolerance relations (composite feature control frames) is out of scope for this stage (design: Out of scope); refused by name, left out of the round trip.
reasons.no part definitions: NIST FTC-08's -tg file is tessellated only: read_part_definitions finds no solid or shell with faces, so there is no part to write to (as for the reader).
reasons.removal refused: The file has PMI of the part the reader did not read (an unread tolerance whose toleranced feature or datum did not resolve, with its measure qualification, pinned in read/findings.json) that references instances the replace removes; kept PMI must not dangle, so the replace is refused naming it (design item 6: anything else blocks). The id_attributes listed beside it would be removed with their items.

patterns.key: specify-core: ISO 286 fit written as its deviations
patterns.reason: specify-core writes each ISO 286 class as the class's deviations only (TOLERANCE_VALUE, no LIMITS_AND_FITS), because OpenCascade writes the grade wrongly (specify-core writer.py; anti-requirement 'ISO 286 grade written wrongly'). haecceity writes the class the intent states as LIMITS_AND_FITS (§5.2.5); the deviations specify-core states are the class's (checked by the reader stage), so the meaning is the class, and haecceity's form is the practice's.

patterns.key: haecceity: ISO 286 fit written as LIMITS_AND_FITS
patterns.reason: The other side of the fit difference: the class written as PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE → LIMITS_AND_FITS(letter, 'hole'/'shaft', grade, '') (§5.2.5), read back as the same class.

patterns.key: haecceity: thread written as its THREAD entity
patterns.reason: specify-core writes threads as 'manufacturing requirement' text and a 'pmi-assist' attribute set because OpenCascade has no thread class (anti-requirement 'threads, knurls … appended as raw text'); haecceity writes the schema's THREAD with its shape_representation_with_parameters (thread WR1–WR16 checked). number_of_threads is written '1.' (one start): what the ratio counts is not settled (design: Status, open); the pitch is kept in the attribute set beside it.

patterns.key: specify-core: 'manufacturing requirement' text note (decision 5: not written)
patterns.reason: specify-core's 'manufacturing requirement' properties (surface texture, edge condition, general tolerance and thread/knurl text) are not a standard AP242 form; maintainer decision 5: not written. The general tolerance is written in its standard 'default tolerances' form and compares equal.

patterns.key: specify-core: thread as a 'pmi-assist' attribute set
patterns.reason: specify-core's user defined attribute set restating the thread (side, designation, pitch, class, hand, drill) because it cannot write THREAD; haecceity writes the THREAD itself and only what is not thread semantics (pitch, tapping drill, depths) as an attribute set.

patterns.key: haecceity: pitch, tapping drill and depths as an attribute set
patterns.reason: Tapping drill diameter and depth and full-thread depth are not thread semantics (design: Threads and knurls): a user defined attribute set on the thread's feature (UDA practice §5–7). The intent's pitch goes there too, since the schema's thread has no pitch item. 'through' is not written: a boolean_representation_item does not read back (reader gap reported).

patterns.key: specify-core: knurl as a 'pmi-assist' attribute set
patterns.reason: The intent states a knurl's pattern, pitch and diameter only; turned_knurl needs 6 to 9 parameters (WR2) and a helix angle for a diamond knurl (WR9), which the intent does not state, so no TURNED_KNURL is written rather than guess them (the case's 'not written' says so). specify-core's attribute set is not reproduced: whether the knurl should be written with assumed standard parameters (DIN 82) is for the maintainer.
The knurled faces are a feature in specify-core's file only because its knurl attribute set is on them; with no knurl written (previous entry) there is no feature on them.

specify-core's file states tolerance magnitudes in metres (5.E-05 m), OpenCascade's unit of the last dimension written (anti-requirement 'tolerance length unit taken from the last dimension written'); haecceity writes each value in the unit the intent states (millimetres). Equal in meaning (compared by meaning above); different as stated.

occt.detail: not in XCAF's metadata, which holds "semantic text" = "Break sharp edges 0.2 max"
occt.reason: XCAF's metadata reader keeps one string per property name on the part's label (TDataStd_NamedData, keyed 'semantic text'), so of several part notes it holds the last. Each note is its own property_definition('semantic text') with its descriptive item, as PMI practice §7.4 defines editable note text (one property per note; its count is 'number of semantic text notes', Table 17) and NIST's files carry (FTC-07: 16, FTC-10: 19). haecceity reads every note back (pmi_write.rs notes_and_surface_textures_are_standard_forms).

occt.detail: #651: value 5.014 vs 10. Millimetre (different); not plus/minus (range true lower_bound 10 upper_bound 0.028)
occt.reason: specify-core's own Ø10 (kept byte for byte by the add, not written by haecceity): '#648 = (... MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(POSITIVE_LENGTH_MEASURE(10.),#633) ... REPRESENTATION_ITEM('nominal value'))', '#651 = DIMENSIONAL_SIZE(#646,'diameter')', '#654 = TOLERANCE_VALUE(#653,#652)' with both bounds below nominal (-0.028, -0.013), '#655 = PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE(#654,#651)'. OpenCascade's known misread of both deviations below nominal (the capture's known_misreads; specify-core writer.py) drops the deviations and garbles the value; haecceity reads 10 mm with the stated deviations. The same instance in the input file is pinned alike (known_pmi.json occt 'thumbwheel_thread_knurl occt dimension 0:1:4:1').
